summary: Lewis County, WA lookout built in 1945 for the Washington Forest Fire Association; removed in 1967; only footings and steps reported later, on permit-only Vail Tree Farm land.

facts.design: 12-foot timber tower with 14 x 14 foot cab (1950 replacement)
facts.status_note: Removed in 1967 per the register and lookout inventory (Firelookout.com says destroyed); later visits found only footings, steps and a moved block
facts.agency: Washington Forest Fire Association (per register); newspaper items show the state DNR opening the post in 1957

access.note: Inside Weyerhaeuser's Vail Tree Farm; a recreation access permit is needed to visit legally

visit.trail_note: A motorized permit allows a drive to the summit; the tower is gone, so there is nothing to climb.

events.note: Built by the Washington Forest Fire Association with Weyerhaeuser's help (38th Annual Report, quoted by Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb). Register describes a 20-foot live-in tower.
12-foot timber tower with 14 x 14 foot cab replaced an earlier tower (Biennial Report of the Forestry Division, as quoted)
Daily Chronicle item (April 15, 1952) says Mr. Challender returned to his job as lookout
Daily Chronicle (July 1957) reports the state DNR Chehalis district opened the Lucas Creek post
Daily Chronicle (June 5, 1964): Mrs. Fred (Rosalie) Hendricks of Onalaska stationed at the lookout
Register and lookout inventory say removed; Firelookout.com says destroyed
Leslie Romer found cement footings around 2003 (per WillhiteWeb; year approximate)
Registered June 18, 2012 as FFLOS US 1284, nominated by Ray Kresek
Visits around 2010 and 2016 found only cement steps and a block that had been moved
WillhiteWeb 2018 visit: scotch broom and blackberry brush hide any remnants

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and lookout inventory say removed in 1967; Firelookout.com says destroyed. The year matches, so the record uses removed.
Register and Firelookout.com give 20 feet for the 1945 tower; the 1950 replacement was 12 feet (about 3.7 m). The record's 3.7 m is the replacement's height.

Register credits the Washington Forest Fire Association; 1957 and 1964 newspaper items show the state DNR opening the post and stationing a lookout there. The record keeps the Association as builder and register agency.

sources.title: Lucas Creek Lookout Site - Vail Tree Farm

notes_for_editor: Construction, replacement and removal year agree across sources; the removed-versus-destroyed wording is the only dispute. Fitzhugh's early-1950s tenure has no firm year, so it is in the story but not in events. The 1957 and 1964 newspaper items were read through the Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb quotations, not the original clippings. LewisTalk is a general piece on Weyerhaeuser land in Lewis County, not on Vail specifically. Register nominator Ray Kresek is recorded only in the event note.
